/-!
# The canonical Poisson bracket on a polynomial algebra in $2n$ variables

For a commutative ring `R` and a finite type `σ`, we equip `MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R`
with its canonical Poisson bracket
$$\{f, g\} = \sum_{i} \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}\frac{\partial g}{\partial y_i}
  - \frac{\partial f}{\partial y_i}\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_i}\right),$$
where $x_i$ (resp. $y_i$) denotes the variable indexed by `Sum.inl i` (resp. `Sum.inr i`).
This is the polynomial algebra underlying the `n`-th *canonical Poisson algebra* $P_n(R)$
when `σ = Fin n`.

Classical sources index the same object by $2n$ variables $X_1, \dots, X_{2n}$ with bracket
$\{f, g\} = \sum_{i=1}^n (\partial f/\partial X_i \cdot \partial g/\partial X_{i+n}
- \partial f/\partial X_{i+n} \cdot \partial g/\partial X_i)$; here `Sum.inl i`
plays the role of $X_i$ and `Sum.inr i` the role of $X_{i+n}$
(see e.g. [AvdE07](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608009), Notations 1).
-/

namespace MvPolynomial

variable {R σ : Type*} [CommRing R] [Fintype σ]

/-- The canonical Poisson bracket on `MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R`, given by
$\{f, g\} = \sum_{i} (\partial_{x_i} f \cdot \partial_{y_i} g
- \partial_{y_i} f \cdot \partial_{x_i} g)$ where $x_i$ (resp. $y_i$) is the variable
indexed by `Sum.inl i` (resp. `Sum.inr i`). -/
noncomputable def poissonBracket (f g : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R) : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R :=
  ∑ i : σ, (pderiv (Sum.inl i) f * pderiv (Sum.inr i) g -
    pderiv (Sum.inr i) f * pderiv (Sum.inl i) g)

@[simp]
theorem poissonBracket_self (f : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R) : poissonBracket f f = 0 :=
  Finset.sum_eq_zero fun i _ => by rw [mul_comm, sub_self]

theorem poissonBracket_swap (f g : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R) :
    poissonBracket f g = -poissonBracket g f := by
  rw [poissonBracket, poissonBracket, ← Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

@[simp]
theorem poissonBracket_X_inl_inl (i j : σ) :
    poissonBracket (X (Sum.inl i) : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R) (X (Sum.inl j)) = 0 :=
  Finset.sum_eq_zero fun k _ => by
    rw [pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inl j : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inr k from by simp),
      pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inl i : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inr k from by simp), mul_zero, zero_mul,
      sub_self]

@[simp]
theorem poissonBracket_X_inr_inr (i j : σ) :
    poissonBracket (X (Sum.inr i) : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R) (X (Sum.inr j)) = 0 :=
  Finset.sum_eq_zero fun k _ => by
    rw [pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inr i : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inl k from by simp),
      pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inr j : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inl k from by simp), zero_mul, mul_zero,
      sub_self]

@[simp]
theorem poissonBracket_X_inl_inr [DecidableEq σ] (i j : σ) :
    poissonBracket (X (Sum.inl i) : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R) (X (Sum.inr j)) =
      if i = j then 1 else 0 := by
  rw [poissonBracket, Finset.sum_eq_single i]
  · rw [pderiv_X_self, one_mul,
      pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inl i : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inr i from by simp), zero_mul, sub_zero]
    rcases eq_or_ne i j with rfl | h
    · simp
    · rw [pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inr j : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inr i from by simpa using Ne.symm h),
        if_neg h]
  · intro k _ hk
    rw [pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inl i : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inl k from by simpa using Ne.symm hk),
      pderiv_X_of_ne (show (Sum.inl i : σ ⊕ σ) ≠ Sum.inr k from by simp)]
    simp
  · simp

@[simp]
theorem poissonBracket_X_inr_inl [DecidableEq σ] (i j : σ) :
    poissonBracket (X (Sum.inr i) : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ σ) R) (X (Sum.inl j)) =
      if i = j then -1 else 0 := by
  rw [poissonBracket_swap, poissonBracket_X_inl_inr]
  split_ifs with h₁ h₂ h₂ <;> simp_all [Ne.symm]

end MvPolynomial

findings.description: In the direct use site FormalConjectures/Arxiv/math.0608009/PoissonConjecture.lean, line 114 calls Alpöge's F a “degree-$6$” counterexample. Its first component contains x^3 y^3 z with coefficient 1 and has total degree 7; the map has degree 7, not 6. I proved ((JacobianConjecture.F ℚ) 0).totalDegree = 7 in /workspace/review/degree.lean without sorry. This does not affect the theorem or the Poisson-bracket definition.
findings.source_evidence: The cited post https://x.com/__alpoge__/status/2079028340955197566 gives the first component as (1+xy)^3 z + y^2(1+xy)(4+3xy). Its degree-7 term x^3 y^3 z cannot cancel against the second summand, whose degree is at most 6. AvdE07, Notations 1, defines the degree of an endomorphism as the maximum total degree of the images of its variables (https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608009).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “degree-$6$ counterexample map” with “degree-$7$ counterexample map”, or omit the degree.

reformulations.difference: The definition checks brackets only on generators and leaves the right-hand side unmapped, rather than requiring the usual Poisson-morphism law {φ(f),φ(g)} = φ({f,g}) for all polynomials.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All generator brackets are 0, 1, or -1 and hence are fixed by every coefficient-algebra endomorphism. Bilinearity and the Leibniz rule extend the generator equations to all polynomials by induction in both arguments. Conversely, specializing the full morphism law to generators gives the definition. /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves this equivalence over every commutative coefficient ring and finite index type and specializes it to the actual use-site definition.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion is Function.Bijective φ rather than explicitly asserting the existence of an inverse Poisson-algebra endomorphism.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A bijective algebra homomorphism gives an algebra equivalence. If φ preserves the bracket, applying φ to the proposed bracket-preservation identity for its inverse proves that identity by injectivity and the inverse equations. Conversely, an algebra equivalence is bijective. The corresponding per-endomorphism equivalence, including bracket preservation by the inverse, is proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical defect was found in any of the seven declarations of the reviewed library module, and no inherited misuse of its definition was found. The formula agrees exactly with AvdE07's canonical bracket. Lean experiments checked empty indices, one coordinate pair, constants, the zero ring, characteristic two, off-diagonal pairings, and nonlinear examples, and proved coefficient-linearity, Leibniz, and Jacobi. The named scratch proofs and all six library lemmas have no sorryAx dependency. Direct bracket evaluation is unavailable because the definition is noncomputable; bracket tests were proved symbolically, with small ZMod arithmetic also checked by decide/#eval. Mathlib has no duplicate Poisson-bracket definition; its Matrix.J has the opposite sign to the generator-bracket matrix, which gives the same symplectic preservation condition. The use-site theorem types retain their CharZero assumptions, and extending the dimension quantifier to n = 0 adds only a true case. Current sources support the recorded solved/open statuses. The arXiv morphism discussion contains apparent dropped-φ and n-versus-2n typographical errors; the generator condition was checked against the standard intertwining law and the intended characterization in Lemma 2. BCW82 was inaccessible behind Cloudflare, but the relevant implication chain was read directly in AvdE07, Theorem 7. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review/; no repository files were modified.
